mathematical_effects.row_permutation: Preserves the conjunction of row equations, but changes the Lagrange-basis placement of row values and generally changes A_j(X), B_j(X), C_j(X), and H(X).
mathematical_effects.a_b_swap: Preserves each row product and its solution set, but exchanges the A/B contributions to the Groth16 queries; it is not identity of proving-query semantics.
mathematical_effects.nonzero_factor_normalization: A <- sA*A, B <- sB*B, C <- sA*sB*C preserves the row zero set. The observed scales are row-dependent and include two orientations/profiles, so no single global rescaling of the query vectors follows.
mathematical_effects.expanded_relation_match: Equality of expanded A*B-C polynomials proves equality of the individual row relation, not equality or a linear correspondence of the A, B, and C factor polynomials used by setup queries.
mathematical_effects.helper_projection: Eliminating T and adding/removing the packed position relation preserves the supported projected relation, but changes the variable/row QAP data; no L/IC/query transformation has been derived.
mathematical_effects.h_query: Both systems have the same domain size and hence the same generic H-query basis shape. Their witness-specific H coefficients/evaluations differ; common basis shape is not proof of A/B/L/IC query compatibility.
